content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Bread most commonly symbolizes God-given life, provision, and spiritual nourishment, understood supremely in Christian teaching as Jesus Christ, the “bread of life.”","primary_basis":["Exodus 16:4-15, 31-35 — manna as bread provided by God in the wilderness.","Deuteronomy 8:3 — bread contrasted with, yet used to illustrate, dependence on every word from God.","John 6:32-35, 48-58 — Jesus identifies himself as the true bread from heaven and the bread of life.","Matthew 26:26-29; Mark 14:22-25; Luke 22:19-20 — Jesus identifies the broken bread of the Last Supper with his body.","1 Corinthians 10:16-17; 11:23-29 — bread signifies participation in Christ’s body and the unity of believers."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The sacramental body or real presence of Christ in the Eucharist. Traditions agree that Eucharistic bread signifies Christ’s body but differ materially over whether and how Christ is objectively present.","basis":["Matthew 26:26","Luke 22:19","John 6:51-58","1 Corinthians 10:16","1 Corinthians 11:23-29"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"God’s word or revealed truth as nourishment for spiritual life.","basis":["Deuteronomy 8:3","Matthew 4:4","Luke 4:4","Jeremiah 15:16"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Ordinary material provision and the necessities of daily life rather than a specifically christological symbol.","basis":["Matthew 6:11","Luke 11:3","Proverbs 30:8-9","Acts 2:46"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The fellowship and corporate unity of the church, represented by many believers sharing or forming one loaf.","basis":["Acts 2:42,46","1 Corinthians 10:17"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Sacred fellowship with God or God’s covenantal presence, especially through the bread of the Presence and sacred meals.","basis":["Exodus 25:23-30","Leviticus 24:5-9","1 Samuel 21:4-6"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Affliction, sorrow, wickedness, or dishonestly obtained sustenance, as in expressions such as “bread of tears,” “bread of wickedness,” or “bread of deceit.”","basis":["Psalm 80:5","Proverbs 4:17","Proverbs 20:17","Isaiah 30:20"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus around bread as life-sustaining provision and spiritual nourishment from God, especially Christ as the bread of life. Bread is nevertheless context-dependent and does not have one exclusive symbolic referent. Eucharistic interpretations are especially prominent but remain divided over the nature of Christ’s presence."}
